meta.test: exact two-sided McNemar on complete pairs, Monte-Carlo conditional on the discordant count
meta.compute: CPU only. No GPU, no RunPod pod. $0.00 of the AXV compute budget.
meta.caveat: Power is computed against FIXED true arm accuracies and INDEPENDENT pairs. Seeds inside one AXV batch share the data shard, the pod and the wall-clock budget, so real within-batch correlation makes the true n_needed larger, not smaller. These are therefore optimistic lower bounds on n.

attenuation_example.note: A true projected-minus-full of -9 tasks over 27 runs is a 33.3 pp deficit and appears as an exact 0 tie when the 12 stopped pairs are dropped. Censoring did not shrink a small effect; it removed every observation that carried it.

test_size_check.note: At n=3 the exact two-sided McNemar test is degenerate: with 3 pairs the smallest attainable p-value is 0.25, so the test can never reject at the 0.05 level no matter how large the true difference. A complete-case n=3 protocol is not a weak test, it is a test that cannot fire.

n3_headline.conclusion: At the n=3 an AXV batch can afford, the exact paired test cannot reject at the 5% level at all (minimum attainable two-sided p is 0.25). Even ignoring that, 80% power against a 10-point difference needs n in the low hundreds, against 20 points n in the tens, and against 40 points n in the twenties. Every null AXV reports from a complete-case n=3 batch is therefore a statement about nothing.
